rules.title: Borrow before you clone
rules.what: Borrow (&T, &str, &[T], Cow) when ownership is not needed; clone only where ownership is genuinely required.
rules.why: A clone written to quiet the borrow checker allocates and copies data that could have been borrowed; in a hot loop it dominates the cost of the work.
rules.how: Take &str/&[T] in signatures, return iterators, use Cow<str> for sometimes-owned values; check allocations with a heap profiler (dhat, heaptrack).

patterns.note: clone() inside a loop body; candidate only, ownership may genuinely be required.

verify.how: Allocation count of the hot path compared before and after, or clippy redundant_clone clean.

rules.title: No intermediate collect()
rules.what: Chain iterators without an intermediate collect(); materialise only the final result, with with_capacity when the size is known.
rules.why: Every collect into a temporary Vec is an allocation and a copy for a value consumed right after.
rules.how: Keep the chain lazy; collect once at the end; pre-size with Vec::with_capacity or extend() into a reused buffer.

patterns.note: collect() immediately re-iterated: the intermediate Vec is avoidable.

verify.how: Each collect() feeds a stored or returned value, not another iterator chain.

rules.title: Never block the async executor
rules.what: Inside async code, do not call std::thread::sleep, block_on or long CPU work; use the runtime's async sleep and spawn_blocking for CPU-bound work.
rules.why: A blocking call parks an executor worker: the other tasks on it freeze, latency grows and the runtime spawns more threads to compensate.
rules.how: tokio::time::sleep, tokio::task::spawn_blocking for CPU work, async I/O; bound channels and JoinSets; propagate cancellation.

patterns.note: Blocking call; harmful only inside async code or on an executor thread.

verify.how: A test with concurrent tasks shows no executor stall (e.g. tokio-console or a latency assertion).

rules.title: Reuse network clients
rules.what: Create one HTTP client (reqwest::Client or equivalent) per service and clone the handle; never build one per request.
rules.why: Client::new() per call loses the connection pool and repeats the TLS handshake on every request.
rules.how: Build the client once (OnceLock, application state) with timeouts; clones share the pool.

patterns.note: Client built here; fine at start-up, a defect inside a handler or loop.

verify.how: The client is built once and shared; requests carry a timeout.

rules.title: Handle expected errors without panicking
rules.what: Return Result and use ? on foreseeable error paths; keep unwrap()/expect() for invariants that are genuinely guaranteed.
rules.why: A panic on an expected error restarts the service: a cold cache, lost in-flight work and computation redone at every incident.
rules.how: Propagate with ?, map errors to typed errors, document each remaining expect() with the invariant it relies on.

patterns.note: unwrap(); acceptable in tests and on proven invariants, candidate on request paths.

verify.how: Remaining unwrap()/expect() calls each guard a documented invariant; clippy unwrap_used clean on request paths.

rules.title: Lean crate graph, release builds
rules.what: Justify each crate, disable unused default features, and ship release builds.
rules.why: Every crate and default feature weighs on compile time, binary size and the maintenance and security surface.
rules.how: default-features = false with explicit features; cargo tree -d for duplicates; cargo build --release (and LTO when measured) for production.

verify.how: cargo tree output reviewed; production artefact built with --release.
